code_review.note: All three planted problems are found and fixed (17 tests pass, and the changes really are left uncommitted), but they sit in a raw JSON dump of 8 findings, the file paths point to a different fixture directory, and user-visible CLI changes (id parsing, list usage errors) were made without asking.

with_skill.note: It fixes all three planted problems in two commits (verified in the code and git log, 14 tests pass), and leaves the user-visible changes open for the owner, each with a recommendation: the raw stack trace on a corrupt file, bare --tag, and the empty id.

without_skill.note: A clear numbered report that fixes all three planted problems (15 tests pass, two commits), but it changed list --tag usage behavior without asking and never mentions that a corrupt file now crashes with a raw SyntaxError.

reason: All three fixed the planted data-loss, store-bypass and console.warn problems, and their claims checked out against the code. Y stood out because it made only the fixes the branch needed and put each user-visible choice to the owner with a recommendation. It also ended with a short, ordered guide on where to look. Z was nearly as clear but made one user-facing change silently and missed the crash it introduced, while X buried the risk in a JSON dump, made several behavior changes unasked, and pointed at the wrong paths.
